60121245.s: Al Uqayr Seaport is an archaeological seaport in Al-Ahsa Governorate, in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. The port lies 65 kilometres from the city of Hofuf, on the western shore of the Arabian Gulf. It is the oldest seaport in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and served as the maritime gateway to the Najd region.

60121244.s: Jawatha Mosque (also spelled Juwatha or Jawatha) is in Al-Ahsa Governorate in eastern Saudi Arabia, about 17 kilometres north-east of the city of Hofuf, within a park of the same name. It was built in the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by the people of the Bahrain region, the Banu Abd al-Qays, who embraced Islam willingly rather than under compulsion. The Prophet praised them, saying: "Honour your brothers, for they are the most like you; they accepted Islam willingly, not under compulsion." The foundations of the mosque still stand today.

60121239.s: The Coffee Museum is a distinctive museum that includes a cafe, a shop and a coffee academy. It also records the history of coffee in Saudi Arabia and displays the tools and methods used to grow, grind and roast it.

60121235.s: Mehaires Palace is in Al-Ahsa Governorate, in eastern Saudi Arabia. It was built by Imam Saud bin Abdulaziz on the top of a hill in 1208 AH for military purposes. It is a small fortress of round towers with a number of rooms, where weapons, supplies and ammunition were stored. The fort witnessed a battle between the Imam's forces and the forces of Zayd bin Urayar, who were driven out of northern Al Mubarraz and the northern villages of Al-Ahsa.

60121231.s: Ibrahim Palace is a historic palace and one of the landmarks of Al-Ahsa in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. It stands north of the Al Koot district and was the main headquarters of the Ottoman garrison in Hofuf, Al-Ahsa, which was then part of Basra. King Abdulaziz Al Saud took it on the night of 5 Jumada al-Awwal 1331 AH (13 April 1913) when he annexed Al-Ahsa.
60121231.b:
Ibrahim Palace is a historic palace and one of the landmarks of Al-Ahsa in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. It stands north of the Al Koot district and was the main headquarters of the Ottoman garrison in Hofuf, Al-Ahsa, which was then part of Basra. King Abdulaziz Al Saud took it on the night of 5 Jumada al-Awwal 1331 AH (13 April 1913) when he annexed Al-Ahsa.

Construction of the palace began together with the Qubba Mosque in 963 AH (1555 AD). Over the following century it expanded to include a fortress, a prison and Ottoman baths. In March 2019 the General Authority for Tourism and National Heritage announced the completion of restoration work on all parts and facilities of the palace. The work included rebuilding collapsed sections, the plasterwork of the palace facilities, and painting the buildings to suit the historic site, as well as levelling the square in front of the palace and preparing it to host tourism events and festivals.

60121230.s: The First Hofuf School, also known as the Princes School or the House of Culture, is a Saudi government school in Hofuf, Al-Ahsa Governorate. Construction began in 1937 and it was officially opened in February 1941 under the patronage of Saud bin Jiluwi, then Emir of Al-Ahsa. It is the oldest government school in Saudi Arabia and is tied to the history and achievements of King Abdulaziz, who founded it as the starting point of education in the Eastern Province. Many officials studied there, including Khalid Al-Faisal, Emir of Makkah, who studied the Quran and the first two primary years in Al-Ahsa.
60121230.b:
The First Hofuf School, also known as the Princes School or the House of Culture, is a Saudi government school in Hofuf, Al-Ahsa Governorate. Construction began in 1937 and it was officially opened in February 1941 under the patronage of Saud bin Jiluwi, then Emir of Al-Ahsa. It is the oldest government school in Saudi Arabia and is tied to the history and achievements of King Abdulaziz, who founded it as the starting point of education in the Eastern Province. Many officials studied there, including Khalid Al-Faisal, Emir of Makkah, who studied the Quran and the first two primary years in Al-Ahsa, the petroleum minister Ali Al-Naimi, and the former labour minister Ghazi Al-Gosaibi.

The Princes School's first graduating class, of 70 students, finished in 1943. Its design is largely Islamic in style, and the eastern entrance was built in the Arab-Islamic architectural tradition. It is among the tourist and archaeological sites listed by the General Authority for Tourism and National Heritage in Al-Ahsa.

The comfortable rooms have traditional Middle Eastern fabrics, furniture and decor, flat-screen TVs, minibars, free Wi-Fi, and tea and coffee makers. Upgraded rooms have separate living areas, while the two-bedroom apartments have kitchens.

60121215.s: Al Jubri Mosque is a historic mosque and archaeological site in the Al Koot district of Hofuf, in Al-Ahsa Governorate in eastern Saudi Arabia. It dates to the ninth century AH, specifically 880 AH, when it was built by Saif bin Zamil bin Hussein Al Jubri, then emir of the Jubrid emirate in Al-Ahsa.

60121190.s: Khuzam Palace is one of the palaces of Al-Ahsa in eastern Saudi Arabia. It was built at the south-western entrance to Hofuf, in the Al Naathil district, between 1207 and 1210 AH in the time of Imam Saud bin Abdulaziz the Great. It was sited there as a military defence against the Bedouin camps that settle in that area at certain times each year, when nomads come to Al-Ahsa to buy their supplies. It is smaller than Ibrahim Palace in Al Koot, with walls measuring about 70 by 80 metres.

60121167.s: Al Asfar Lake lies in Al Umran, east of Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia. It is the largest body of water in the Gulf region and the only one of its kind in the Kingdom that supports complete wildlife. It was formerly called Hajar Lake. The lake is very important: it absorbs excess water from heavy rains and protects the area from swamps through open drains. It is also a livelihood for local people and a source of grasses used as fodder for livestock, small fish, and plants used in manufacturing such as rushes.
60121167.b: Al Asfar Lake lies in Al Umran, east of Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia. It is the largest body of water in the Gulf region and the only one of its kind in the Kingdom that supports complete wildlife. It was formerly called Hajar Lake. The lake is very important: it absorbs excess water from heavy rains and protects the area from swamps through open drains. It is also a livelihood for local people and a source of grasses used as fodder for livestock, small fish, and plants used in manufacturing such as rushes. In addition, it has been a natural habitat for many resident and migratory animals and birds, and Al Asfar Lake in the Al-Ahsa oasis is the only lake in the Kingdom that supports complete wildlife. In February 2019 the Saudi Ministry of Environment announced that the lake would be turned into a nature reserve, with the aim of preparing it for inclusion on the World Heritage List.

60121164.s: Al-Taraf Model Park, also known as the Al-Ahsa zoo, is a park with many animals, including predators such as lions and tigers, tame animals such as giraffes, mountain goats and deer, birds of prey such as falcons and eagles, and domestic birds such as pelicans, pigeons and ducks. There is also a reptile house with crocodiles and snakes. The park has some children's rides, as well as many fountains and artificial waterfalls among palm trees and green spaces.

60121163.s: Jawatha Tourist City in Al-Ahsa is an entertainment destination near the historic Jawatha Mosque, where the second Friday prayer in Islam was held. It offers many activities for children and adults, such as an amusement park, a paragliding club, a karting club, a paintball club, and a lake with boats. It also contains the Hajar Heritage Souq, spaces for live, heritage and cultural events, and areas for winter camping.

60121161.s: Al-Qara Hill, also known as Jabal Al-Shabaan, lies between the villages of Al-Tuwaithir and Al-Qara in Al-Ahsa Governorate, in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. It is one of the most prominent natural attractions in Al-Ahsa and was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2018 when the Al-Ahsa Oasis was added. The hill is 15 kilometres east of the city of Hofuf and contains caves, known locally as maghara. Some of them, such as Al-Nashab Cave, keep a mild, almost constant temperature throughout the year.

60121094.s: Ain Umm Sab'a, also called Ain Muhallam, is a freshwater spring with a flow estimated at twenty thousand gallons per minute. It lies north of the city of Al Mubarraz, near the village of Al Qarin in Al-Ahsa Governorate in eastern Saudi Arabia. Residents and visitors from the Arabian Gulf come here for leisure and therapeutic purposes, and it is one of the area's most important water sources. The spring covers an area of 1,200 m3, and the water temperature is 104 degrees Celsius in the middle and 101 degrees at the edges.

Ain Umm Sab'a is considered an ideal place for leisure tourism and health tourism, thanks to its natural setting, good climate, the wide palm oases around it, fresh air and green gardens. This has made it a tourist destination on the Al-Ahsa tourism map for visitors from within Saudi Arabia and from all the Gulf states. The water at the edges of the lake reaches 101 degrees Celsius, while in the middle it reaches 104 degrees. The lake's water is warm, and many visitors come in winter to enjoy the hot water and spend relaxing time in nature among the palm farms.

60121092.s: Ain Al-Harrah is one of the springs of Al-Ahsa Governorate, Saudi Arabia. It lies in the city of Al Mubarraz and is a medium-sized spring, named for the heat of the water that flows from it. It is close to the Al Mubarraz cemetery. Its water is said to flow at about twenty thousand gallons per minute and reaches the surface through three outlets, forming a large lake, on which the Irrigation and Drainage Authority installed large pumps after its water decreased.
